text:
carmen: Heads-up — I'm planning a staggered enable for the prefetch+batching toggle (prefetch_window_v2). Goal: reduce cold KV miss rate without hurting p99 latency. Will start with a small rolling cohort this afternoon.

jia: SGTM. What's the initial audience and duration?

carmen: 2% of traffic, region windowing: na-west only, 30m observation window, then 10% if stable. Canary slice = low-rps hosts only.

sam: Can you add the exact rollback criteria? Also pinging @vinh for observability dashboards.

carmen: Rollback triggers: p99 increase > 20ms sustained over 3 consecutive 5m buckets OR error rate > 0.5% (client 5xx). If either fires we flip flag off and route back to prefetch_window_v1.

vinh: I'll add dashboards and a short alert. Key KPIs: p50/p95/p99 latency, req/sec, kv_miss_rate, cpu GPU util, and end-to-end error rate. I'll set an auto-snooze of alerts for 10m after toggle changes to avoid noise.

sana: Please include cost delta metric — even a small increase in tokens or calls can matter.

carmen: Good call. We'll track token_per_req and billing_estimate.

sam: Code-review ping: PR 4321 is the flag + toggle wiring. @jia can you review the gating logic? Link: https://git.company/repo/pull/4321

jia: On it, aiming for review in the next hour. Two quick asks: 1) make the audience selector pluggable by region, 2) add a debug sampling header so we can trace requests that hit the new code path.

carmen: Both added in the latest commit. Example header: X-Prefetch-Debug: cohort=na-west-2pct;trace=1

deploy-bot: deploy queued: env=staging, toggle=prefetch_window_v2, cohort=2%, region=na-west, initiated_by=carmen

vinh: Prometheus queries I'll watch (glance):
```
rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="runtime",le="0.2"}[5m])
sum(rate(redwood_inference_errors_total[5m])) by (code)
```
Also adding a simple composite graph for kv_miss_rate vs p99 latency.

carmen: After the 30m observation we'll post a short status update one of: OK -> progress to 10%, Degraded -> rollback. I'll keep the thread updated.

sam: Add a note in the oncall handover doc if we leave the cohort running overnight.

carmen: Will do. Runbook link: <https://wiki.company/runbooks/prefetch-window-ff> (section: canary + rollback).

jia: Quick question about traffic split — do we need to carve by customer ID or by host? Host-based is easiest but may bias latency distributions.

carmen: We chose host-based for this first rollout to reduce blast radius of heavy customers. If this looks stable we'll switch to hashed-customer for broader coverage.

deploy-bot: deploy started: toggle=prefetch_window_v2 cohort=2% region=na-west

vinh: Alerts applied: p99-latency-high (threshold 20ms delta), error-rate-high (0.5%), kv-miss-surge (2x). I also created a temporary dashboard link: https://dash.company/d/abcd1234/prefetch-window-canary

sam: Thx. I'll watch oncall channel. If anything odd, I'll flip the flag manually and post rationale here. :thumbsup:

carmen: Update at +20m: no alert, p99 +3ms, kv_miss_rate down ~15%. continuing to 30m.

jia: Reviewed and left two non-blocking comments on PR 4321. Approving now.

carmen: +30m: still green. Moving to 10% cohort in na-west and na-east windowed to low-rps hosts, 1h observation.

deploy-bot: cohort update: toggle=prefetch_window_v2 cohort=10% regions=na-west,na-east initiated_by=carmen

vinh: Dashboard link updated. Watchlist: p99, error-rate, kv_miss_rate, request_rate.

sana: Cost delta showing +2% in the first 15m sample, acceptable.

carmen: Will post final summary after 1h. Thanks all for quick responses.

sam: Nice work — please tag me if you want a formal postmortem entry or rollout note.

carmen: Will do.
